title: What the Correction Percentage Acts On for an Auto Loans Borrower Who Banks With Us
content:
Two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account settle what the correction percentage acts on when a late charge on a loan of the Auto Loans line is put right. The first is whether the borrower holds an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes. The second is whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

## Input, judgement, output

**Input:** the posted balance on the borrower's active checking account, measured against the fee-waiver daily balance published for that account's tier, and the count of recurring deposits posted to that account in the last three months.

**Judgement:** how many of the two readings hold.

**Output:**

- Where both hold, the percentage acts on the scheduled installment less the payments credited to the loan in the current calendar month.
- Where exactly one of the two holds, the percentage acts on the scheduled installment alone.
- Where neither holds, the percentage acts on the scheduled installment together with the charges standing unpaid on the loan.

## The combinations set out

| Posted balance at least the tier's fee-waiver daily balance | At least 2 recurring deposits in the last three months | What the percentage acts on |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the scheduled installment less the payments credited to the loan in the current calendar month |
| yes | no | the scheduled installment alone |
| no | yes | the scheduled installment alone |
| no | no | the scheduled installment together with the charges standing unpaid on the loan |

## How the two readings are taken

The balance reading is taken against the fee-waiver daily balance published for the tier of Personal Checking that the borrower's active account belongs to, so two borrowers with the same balance may read differently where their checking tiers differ.

The deposit reading counts recurring deposits posted to that same checking account in the last three months. A borrower with exactly 2 such deposits meets the reading; a borrower with 1 does not.

## Two ways to the middle outcome

The middle outcome is reached from either side. A borrower with a high balance and no recurring deposits and a borrower with two recurring deposits and a low balance arrive at the same acting base, the scheduled installment alone.
